edition.notes: Cited here by printed page. Hauler prints the palimpsest text with expanded abbreviations in parentheses, editorial supplements in square brackets, marginal folio and quire references, and a critical apparatus at the foot of each page recording the manuscript readings he corrected. The apparatus at p. 106 records that the manuscript reads extendis where the text prints extendit, and it cites Achelis, Hammond, and Rahmani for that correction.
edition.publication: Lipsiae: in aedibus B. G. Teubneri, 1900
edition.title: Hauler, Didascaliae apostolorum fragmenta Veronensia Latina, fasciculus prior

passages.context: Read visually at the page image. The page carries the eucharistic dialogue in the form 'Dominus vobiscum' / 'Et cum spiritu tuo'; 'Susum corda' / 'Habemus ad dominum'; 'Gratias agamus domino' / 'Dignum et iustum est'; and then the opening of the anaphora: 'Gratias tibi referimus, Deus, per dilectum puerum tuum Iesum Christum, quem in ultimis temporibus misisti nobis salvatorem et redemptorem et angelum voluntatis tuae; qui est verbum tuum inseparabilem, per quem omnia fecisti et bene placitum tibi fuit; misisti de caelo in matricem virginis, quique in utero habitus incarnatus est et filius tibi ostensus est ex spiritu sancto et virgine natus; qui voluntatem tuam conplens et populum sanctum tibi adquirens extendit manus, cum pateretur, ut a passione liberaret eos, qui in te crediderunt; qui cumque traderetur voluntariae passioni, ut mortem soluat et vincula diaboli dirumpat et infernum ...'
passages.notes: The apparatus on the same page records that the manuscript reads 'extendis' where the text prints 'extendit', with the correction attributed to Hammond and Rahmani and the German of Achelis cited. This passage witnesses the Latin of the church order conventionally called the Apostolic Tradition; it does not settle that work's authorship, date, or provenance, all of which remain disputed.

passages.context: Read visually at the page image. The page continues and completes the anaphora: '... calcet et iustos inluminet et terminum figat et resurrectionem manifestet, accipiens panem gratias tibi agens dixit: Accipite, manducate: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis confringetur. Similiter et calicem dicens: Hic est sanguis meus, qui pro vobis effunditur; quando hoc facitis, meam commemorationem facitis. Memores igitur mortis et resurrectionis eius offerimus tibi panem et calicem gratias tibi agentes, quia nos dignos habuisti adstare coram te et tibi ministrare. Et petimus, ut mittas spiritum tuum sanctum in oblationem sanctae ecclesiae; in unum congregans des omnibus, qui percipiunt, sanctis in repletionem spiritus sancti ad confirmationem fidei in veritate, ut te laudemus et glorificemus per puerum tuum Iesum Christum, per quem tibi gloria et honor, patri et filio cum sancto spiritu, in sancta ecclesia tua et nunc et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.'
passages.notes: The anaphora as printed has no Sanctus and no intercessions. That absence is a fact about this witness and about the reconstruction of the church order, not about any later rite. This passage witnesses the Latin text; it does not settle the authorship, date, or provenance of the underlying work.

work.author: Edmund Hauler
work.description: Hauler's edition of the Latin fragments of the Verona palimpsest LV(53), printing the Latin Didascalia together with the surviving Latin of the church order conventionally called the Apostolic Tradition or Traditio apostolica. The anaphora at the editor's chapters LXIX-LXX is the oldest surviving Latin text of that prayer and is the witness on which comparisons with the postconciliar second Eucharistic Prayer rest. Authorship, date, place, and redactional history of the underlying church order are disputed and this record takes no position on them.
work.title: Didascaliae apostolorum fragmenta Veronensia Latina. Accedunt canonum qui dicuntur apostolorum et aegyptiorum reliquiae
